requirements.name: profile-csv-file
requirements.text:
Build a command-line tool that profiles a CSV file. For every column it infers a type and reports
row, null, and distinct counts, the minimum and maximum, and for numeric columns the sum, mean, and
median.

requirements.name: list-frequent-values
requirements.text: It also lists the most frequent values of one column.

requirements.name: go-stdlib-build
requirements.text:
Implement in Go 1.22 or newer using only the standard library. The application root is a Go
module, and its executable is the main package at `./cmd/csvstat`.

requirements.name: test-entry
requirements.text:
The completed application provides a POSIX-compatible `bin/test.sh` that runs `go vet ./...` and
`go test ./...` from the application root and exits zero only when both pass.

requirements.name: run-harness-scoring
requirements.text: `drydock uat` runs `sh sources/run.sh` from the completed application root and takes its exit code and output as the score.

requirements.name: command-arguments
requirements.text: Options precede the file. Exactly one file is required.

requirements.name: column-option
requirements.text: Profile only the named column.

requirements.name: read-csv-file
requirements.text:
The file is UTF-8 CSV as RFC 4180 defines it, read with Go's `encoding/csv`. The first record
is the header.

requirements.name: trim-values
requirements.text:
Every header name and every value is trimmed of leading and trailing spaces before any other
rule applies.

requirements.name: reject-malformed-file
requirements.text:
The file is **rejected** when it is empty, when a header name is empty or repeated, or when any
record has a different number of fields from the header.

requirements.name: null-values
requirements.text:
**Null.** A value is null when it is empty, or when it equals `NA`, `N/A`, or `NULL` ignoring
case. All other values are non-null.

requirements.name: type-inference
requirements.text: A column's type is the first of these that every non-null value satisfies:

requirements.name: empty-column-type
requirements.text: A column with no non-null values has type `empty`.

requirements.name: profile-output-rows
requirements.text:
Header `column,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median`, then one row per column in file
order (or the one named by `--column`).

requirements.name: profile-counts
requirements.text: `rows` | Number of data records. | `nulls` | Number of null values. | `distinct` | Number of different non-null values, compared as exact strings after trimming.

requirements.name: profile-min-max
requirements.text: `min`, `max` | `integer`: the smallest and largest value as an integer. `number`: as a decimal. `date`: earliest and latest. `boolean`: `false` if any value is false, else `true`; `true` if any value is true, else `false`. `text`: smallest and largest by byte value. `empty`: empty.

requirements.name: numeric-stats
requirements.text: `sum` | `integer`: the integer total. `number`: the decimal total. Otherwise empty. | `mean` | `integer` and `number`: total divided by non-null count. Otherwise empty. | `median` | `integer` and `number`: the middle value of the sorted non-null values, or the mean of the two middle values when the count is even. Otherwise empty.

requirements.name: decimal-formatting
requirements.text:
**Decimals.** Every `number` `min`, `max`, and `sum`, and every `mean` and `median`, is written with
exactly two decimal places, rounded half away from zero from the exact value, with a leading `-`
when negative and no thousands separator: `1012.50`, `-12.21`, `0.00`. Integer `min`, `max`, and
`sum` are written as plain integers.

requirements.name: frequency-output
requirements.text:
Header `value,count`, then one row per distinct non-null value of the column, ordered by count
descending, then value ascending by byte value, at most `--top` rows. Null values are not listed. A
column with no non-null values writes only the header.

requirements.name: csv-output-format
requirements.text:
CSV on standard output with `\n` line endings. A field that contains a comma, a double quote, or a
newline is quoted as RFC 4180 specifies; Go's `encoding/csv` writer produces this format.

requirements.name: failure-output
requirements.text:
A failing command writes nothing to standard output and one diagnostic line to standard error naming
the file and, for a rejected record, its line number.

requirements.name: exit-codes
requirements.text: | `0` | Success. | `1` | Operational failure: the file cannot be opened or read. | `2` | Usage error: missing or extra file, unknown option, missing option value, `--top` not a positive integer, `--top` without `--freq`, `--column` with `--freq`. | `3` | Rejected: empty file, empty or repeated header name, ragged record, or a column name that is not in the header.

requirements.name: header-only-input
requirements.text: sku,price,in_stock

requirements.name: reject-ragged-record
requirements.text:
sku,price,in_stock
A1,9.99,true
A2,4.50,false
A3,1.25,true,extra
A4,3.00,false

requirements.name: build-executable
requirements.text: Builds ./cmd/csvstat with `go build`

requirements.name: profile-all-columns
requirements.text: A. Every column of each data file

requirements.name: profile-one-column
requirements.text: B. One column

requirements.name: frequencies
requirements.text: C. Frequencies

requirements.name: reject-input-and-failures
requirements.text: E. Rejected input and operational failures

requirements.name: usage-errors
requirements.text: U. Usage errors

requirements.name: grader-gate
requirements.text: Exit 0 only when the build succeeds and every check passes.
